summary: A recording that kept its clicks gets a zoom round each burst of them with one command, in the Clip menu and on the clip's right-click. Clicks too far apart for one still frame now get a zoom that follows the pointer, so no click is cropped out.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Needs a screen recording made in Photonz with some clicks in it (File > New Recording, click around, stop). Checked by the walks zooms-suggested-from-clicks-walk and add-zooms-from-clicks-clip-menu-walk on the probe, which script two clicks into the sample recording.

try.do: Open a screen recording you made in Photonz that has clicks in it, and pick its clip on the timeline.
Right-click the clip and choose Add Zooms from Clicks (it is in the Clip menu too).
Put the playhead just before the first click: the picture is partway into the zoom.
Put the playhead on the clicks: the picture is fully zoomed on where you clicked.
Drag a zoom bar on the Zoom lane, or drag its ends, to move or trim it like any zoom.
Press Command-Z once: every zoom the command made goes.
Open a recording with no clicks and look at Clip > Add Zooms from Clicks: it is greyed.

evaluate: Does a zoom arrive early enough before your first click that you see the click land?
Clicks within two and a half seconds share one zoom. Does that split your recording into the moments you would have picked?
When your clicks jump across the screen, does the zoom that follows the pointer feel smooth, or would you rather have two separate zooms?
Is Add Zooms from Clicks the name you would look for?
rough: The command was already in the app as Suggest Zooms; this renames it to the name settled on the card on 2026-10-20 and fixes the framing. Agents still call it by its old id, suggest_zooms.
No mock covers automatic zooms (video-zoom-wt.html is the manual punch-in), so there is no mock frame to compare against.
The walk's picture of the right-click menu is cut off by the window edge and does not show the row, so it is left out; the walks choose the row by name in both menus and check the zoom it made.
Clicks that need a following zoom use 160% and the pointer path kept beside the recording. Clicks added by hand with no path, spread too wide for any frame tighter than about 110%, get no zoom.
The Zoom added notice stays up for its few seconds after Command-Z has taken the zoom away.
